A company's cash runway is the amount of time it would take to burn through its cash reserves at its current cash burn rate. As at September 2026, Bonterra Resources had cash of CA$15m and no debt. On the latest view, the narrative fair value of Arista Networks at $169.91 sits only slightly above the last close of $167.62. That small gap puts the focus squarely on how sustainable the current AI buildout looks rather than on any big pricing mismatch.

Arista reported Q3 revenue of $3.66 billion, up 58.5%, and forecast Q4 revenue between $3.9 billion and $4 billion. The headline is strong. One table in the 10-Q adds a detail worth holding next to it. Deferred revenue fell in the quarter, from $6,865.9 million to $6,839.5 million. A year earlier it rose $624.5 million. Revenue recognized from the opening deferred balance was $1,715.0 million, about 47% of Q3 revenue, against $699.7 million, about 30%, in Q3 2025. That balance holds multi-year support contracts and product deferrals tied to acceptance clauses. When large customers accept deployments, revenue comes out of it, so part of Q3's growth likely came from earlier shipments clearing rather than only from new orders. New deferrals were still $1,688.6 million, up from $1,324.2 million a year earlier. The balance is being refilled, just not faster than it's being drawn down. The CFO warned against reading one quarter too closely: "the deferred balance can move significantly on a quarterly basis, independent of underlying business drivers." I agree, and this isn't a bear case. Management's first look at 2027 is 38% to 40% growth, to about $18.5 billion. Arista expects $8.6 billion of revenue from remaining performance obligations, about 91% of it within two years, and purchase commitments rose to $11.4 billion from $9.7 billion in Q2. What I'd watch in the Q4 report is whether the balance grows again. If it does alongside revenue of $3.9 billion or more, demand is outrunning acceptances. If it falls again, growth is leaning harder on the balance, and the 2027 range carries more of the story. The Q3 call and both filings are here.
